firstSection.copytitle: Keeping Websites Accessible,Secure, and Easy to Use
firstSection.text:
Building on my experience in developing and improving websites, I am currently deepening my understanding of cybersecurity while applying what I have learned through hands-on experience.
I believe that a website’s value does not end when it goes live; it grows through ongoing maintenance, operation, and continuous improvement. I aim to contribute to the long-term quality and improvement of websites by helping create web experiences that are secure, reliable, and easy to use for everyone.

faq.question: What kind of experience do you have in web development?
faq.answer:
I have worked across a wide range of web-related projects, from backend development to website production.

Before 2016, I worked in backend development, where I was responsible for analyzing issues, identifying their root causes, and finding practical solutions.
In 2016, I transitioned to website development because I wanted to work not only on the underlying systems, but also on the user experience and visual aspects of websites.

faq.question: What were your responsibilities in website development?
faq.answer:
I handled website development, WordPress integration, deployment, and maintenance.

Based on design files created in Adobe Illustrator, I hand-coded websites from scratch, integrated them with WordPress, and handled the process through to deployment.
Working from requests and requirements provided by directors, I translated them into technical requirements, analyzed issues based on the site's structure, and proposed and implemented appropriate solutions.
As I was often the only person responsible for technical work, I also handled a wide range of technical matters beyond development, including maintenance, troubleshooting, and urgent issues.

faq.question: What do you focus on when designing and implementing websites?
faq.answer:
I focus on consistency across the entire site and long-term maintainability when designing and implementing websites.

Rather than simply building websites that are intuitive and easy to use, I try to understand the principles and rules behind both the design and implementation, and reflect them consistently throughout the site.
By organizing and structuring information, using semantic markup, and building reusable components and structures, I aim to create websites that are easier to maintain and improve over time.
Through my studies for the Web Design Skills Test, a national certification in Japan, I also developed an understanding of W3C web standards and WCAG principles.
I apply these concepts to my work by considering responsive design, cross-browser differences, and accessibility, with the goal of creating websites that are as accessible and usable as possible.

faq.question: What kind of work did you do to improve website quality after launch?
faq.answer:
I continuously worked to maintain and improve website quality after launch.

Websites continue to evolve after launch through ongoing content updates and feature additions, creating new challenges and opportunities for improvement.
My post-launch work included resolving issues that arose during ongoing operations and continuously improving website performance.
Rather than simply addressing individual issues, I focused on improvements that considered long-term maintainability and overall quality, helping ensure that websites remain reliable, accessible, and easy to use over time.

My post-launch work included the following:

  • ・Content updates and feature additions
  • ・WordPress and PHP version upgrades
  • ・Log analysis when issues occurred
  • ・Page speed optimization
  • ・Web accessibility improvements, including UI/UX

faq.question: In addition to web development, what responsibilities did you have related to internal IT and infrastructure?
faq.answer:
In addition to my production responsibilities, I was responsible for the company’s internal IT systems and participated in strategic planning meetings.

  • ・Managed servers, domains, and subdomains through hosting providers such as Sakura Internet, Mixhost, and XServer
  • ・Evaluated, selected, and configured server environments
  • ・Installed and configured databases and PHP
  • ・Investigated issues by analyzing alerts and logs and identifying potential causes
  • ・Coordinated with server providers and external freelancers to resolve technical issues
  • ・Provided technical support and guidance to directors and junior team members
  • ・Introduced and configured Slack for internal communication
  • ・Set up and configured XAMPP for local development and testing

faq.question: Which industries have you worked with the most?
faq.answer:
Most of my experience has been in healthcare and social welfare, followed by manufacturing and construction.

Before my previous company was established, its founders were involved in healthcare consulting, which led to many hospital website projects.
I also worked on web systems for the social welfare sector at another company, and my first web development job as a part-time employee was also in the welfare field.
Having a developmental disability myself, I have also had a personal connection to the welfare field since I was a student and have continued to learn about disability-related issues through books and other resources.

faq.question: What direction do you want to take your career in?
faq.answer:
I would like to build on my experience in development, operations, and maintenance while continuing to deepen my knowledge of cybersecurity.

I would like to build on the experience I have gained through continuously addressing challenges and improving websites after they go live, and further develop my technical expertise.
In the long term, I hope to deepen my understanding of the techniques used to attack digital content and the vulnerabilities they exploit, and become an engineer capable of implementing effective technical measures to protect against these threats.

VisualThinking.text:
As part of exploring my personal roots, I have published a research article on the "Community of Mixed-Heritage Orphans in 1970s Nagoya and Its Cultural Evolution", a history my grandparents were closely involved in.

Given the sensitive nature of this topic, I approached the research with strict objectivity, prioritizing diverse viewpoints.
I gathered a wide range of sources, from rare books to international research papers, carefully cross-checking them to ensure historical accuracy.

Through this project, I learned to view individual events not as detached points, but as elements connected to a larger surface, mapping them within a broader social and structural context.
This structural thinking directly translate into my web development work today.
In my daily practice, I rely on official Google documentation and technical community insights to ensure reliable system operation, maintenance, and optimization.

At the same time, I love using creative medium as a language to express my inner state and connect deeply.
On my days off, drawing inspiration from zines and museum visits, I have worked on various projects, including image processing, digital art, video editing, and creative coding.
I am particularly drawn to spirituality and the inner world, continuously researching and reinterpreting.
